dimension: the identity-access TokenMinter and TotpCodeVerifier, and the fourteenth adapter directory that holds them
howToReproduce: Apply the `from` -> `to` replacement in `file`, run `command`, and observe the named case(s) fail. Restore. NO ENTRY NEEDS DOCKER: this directory holds no vendor client, so every suite it drives runs on any machine with node and pnpm, and the two composition suites drive an unroutable PostgreSQL and Redis on purpose. A `pnpm build:v1` entry LEAVES A BROKEN dist BEHIND when it fails, and the next vitest run resolves the workspace package through that dist -- rebuild between entries or a later entry records failures that belong to the previous one's wreckage. That was observed on the first sweep of this ledger and is the reason the driver rebuilds after every build-command entry.
notes: NOTHING SURVIVED UNEXPLAINED. Two entries are DECLARED UNFALSIFIABLE with a measured reason and neither is a shrug: `verify-constant-time-primitive-replaced` is a timing property a value-based suite cannot see, and `port-satisfaction-obligation-dropped` is a PRE-EXISTING hole in the composition root's compile-time proof that this sweep FOUND and that affects all fifty-one bindings rather than this tranche's two. Both are written out in full below.

ONE MUTATION WAS WITHDRAWN AS VACUOUS RATHER THAN COUNTED AS A SURVIVOR. `identity-access-assembled-anyway` guarded the `unassembled.push` for identity-access on `postgres !== undefined`, which is TRUE in every case the suite drives -- the fully-declared install constructs `postgres-tenancy` against an unresolvable host and gets an object anyway -- so it changed no behaviour and was not a mutation at all. It is not in the entry list; `identity-access-declared-assembled`, which deletes the push outright, replaces it and IS killed.

NO ENTRY IS KILLED BY AN ASSERTION COMPARING TWO THINGS THIS TRANCHE CONTROLS. The eleven width entries are killed against `internal-packages/tenancy-database/src/auth.ts`, `apps/agent/src/oauth/oauth.service.ts` and three further extraction-source files, none of which this tranche edits and all of which are byte-identical between `v1` and `origin/main`. The algorithm entries are killed against RFC 4226 Appendix D and RFC 6238 Appendix B, which are outside this repository entirely, and against eighteen answers recorded from the extraction source's own `generateTotp`. The base32 entries are killed against RFC 4648 §10. The composition entries are killed by gates whose expectations are derived from the generator's `ADAPTERS` table and the filesystem.

THE `verify-returns-on-first-match` ENTRY IS THE ONE THIS LEDGER WAS HARDEST TO MAKE HONEST. "It does not early-exit" is normally unfalsifiable by value: with one matching candidate the two implementations agree exactly. A secret whose codes COLLIDE at two adjacent counters was searched for (652,483 draws of a 20-byte secret) and confirmed against the extraction source's `generateTotp`, and with it the two disagree on the RETURNED COUNTER rather than on timing. That is why this entry is a kill and `verify-constant-time-primitive-replaced` is not.

TWO ENTRIES MUTATE A TEST RATHER THAN PRODUCTION CODE, and they are the controls on the control. `extractor-misses-the-inline-mint-sites` and `extractor-reads-one-file-instead-of-five` break the parser that reads the extraction source, and both are killed by the non-vacuity cases in the same file -- the pinned site count and the prefix-set comparison against `TOKEN_PREFIXES`. Without them, a regex that silently matched nothing would have made all eleven width comparisons pass while proving nothing, which is this programme's first lesson arriving in a new disguise.

THE TWO CANARY GATES ARE MUTATED TOO. `generator-adoption-removed` un-adopts the project and `gen-v1-skeleton --check` fails CLOSED -- the two released placeholders reappear MISSING and the eleven real files become EXTRA -- and `census-row-removed` / `census-row-understated` show the test-case census refusing an unpinned package and an understated pin by one case. A pin that could be lowered to match reality is not a pin.

entries.measuredReason: `timingSafeEqual(a, b)` and `a === b` return the SAME boolean for every input this suite can construct; they differ only in how long the comparison takes, and a unit case that asserted a timing difference would be a flake rather than a guard. The property is real and the mutation is real -- replacing the primitive is exactly the regression that would reintroduce a compare-loop oracle on the six digits -- but nothing in a value-based suite can observe it. Its TWIN, `verify-length-guard-removed`, IS killed: that half of the primitive's contract (it THROWS on unequal lengths) is observable, so the pair together shows precisely where the constant-time choice is guarded and where it is only stated.

entries.measuredReason: Deleting the OBLIGATION -- the `readonly "tokenmint-totp:TotpCodeVerifier"` member of the `PortSatisfaction` interface -- while leaving its `true` in the frozen table changes nothing observable, and this was MEASURED against both enforcers rather than assumed: `pnpm build:v1` is green because `Object.freeze({...})` infers its type parameter from the literal and the outer annotation is applied to `Readonly<T>`, so TypeScript's excess-property check never runs on the extra key; and `scripts/arch/composition-root.mjs` is green because its rule reads the KEYS of the frozen literal (`/export const PORT_SATISFACTION[^=]*=\s*Object\.freeze\(\{([\s\S]*?)\}\);/`) and never parses the interface at all. THIS IS A PRE-EXISTING HOLE IN THE COMPOSITION ROOT'S COMPILE-TIME PROOF AND IT AFFECTS ALL FIFTY-ONE BINDINGS EQUALLY, not only this tranche's two -- the same deletion on `keyring-envelope:Hasher` survives identically. It is DECLARED rather than fixed because both available fixes belong to code this tranche does not own: adding `satisfies PortSatisfaction` inside the freeze, or removing the outer annotation, both break the gate's own regex, and widening the gate to parse the interface is a change to `composition-root.mjs` and its pinned control suite. WHAT IS STILL PROVEN: the opposite deletion is killed by `tsc` (`port-satisfaction-value-dropped`), and the substantive claim -- that the adapter really implements the port -- is killed by `tsc` too (`adapter-stops-extending-the-verifier-port`), so the binding is not unguarded; only this one way of deleting its statement is.
